source.title: Escaping Plato’s Cave: Towards the Alignment of 3D and Text Latent Spaces
source.authors: Souhail Hadgi; Luca Moschella; Andrea Santilli; Diego Gomez; Qi-Xing Huang; E. Rodolà; S. Melzi; M. Ovsjanikov

record.file_problem: None; the paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly compares 3D and text representations and evaluates whether they can be aligned, using CKA and cross-modal matching and retrieval rather than a scale sweep.
record.gate_note: The study reports raw and affine-aligned CKA, plus matching and retrieval results after several alignment methods. It does not test whether alignment rises as models get larger or more capable. Figures 2 and 3 provide pair-specific CKA values only as figures; the text also describes the overall patterns. The paper cites results from other work on vision-text alignment, which are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study applies the convergence question to a new modality pair, 3D shape encoders and text encoders. It measures unaligned and affine-aligned CKA and post-hoc linear mappability through matching and retrieval. It finds unimodal 3D encoders align only weakly with text, unlike the vision–text results it cites, and that alignment mainly tracks shared training with CLIP. There is no scale sweep and no image–caption test.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors conclude 3D encoders, unlike vision and text encoders, did not converge to text-like structure (max unimodal CKA 0.12). They also find similarity concentrates in low-dimensional CCA subspaces that global comparisons obscure, and that model complexity does not drive 3D–text alignment.
record.recipe_differences: This is a post-training 3D-text alignment study, not a scale or capability sweep. It uses linear CKA, anchor-based affine translation, local CKA, and CCA subspace projection; alignment tasks include matching and retrieval.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with alignment method and downstream task: affine translation is reported as particularly effective for matching, while local CKA is stronger for top-5 retrieval. The optimal subspace dimension varies by encoder, and performance responds to anchor-set size before plateauing.

fits_no_version.finding: CCA subspaces make the text space more correlated with geometric (Chamfer) distances, and the 3D space more semantic. Multimodal-encoder subspaces do not correlate with geometry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Modalities share only low-dimensional subspaces, while each retains modality-specific (geometric vs semantic) structure.

record.problems: The evaluation uses Objaverse-LVIS and a query set of 500, with results averaged over 3 seeds; no error bars or significance tests are reported in the provided text. The study does not test scaling or capability trends and tests 3D-text rather than image-caption alignment.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 results for RoBERTa and BERT text encoders, Supplementary Tables 2 and 3, and the additional dimension and anchor-count curves were not extracted because of the 60-row limit; the retained rows cover the CLIP comparison, the pairwise CKA figures, and the principal alignment-method outcomes.

untested.parts: No sweep over model size, data scale or capability. Only three 3D architectures of differing complexity are compared, at one data scale.
Entire version: no image–caption or vision-encoder comparison. Vision–text CKA is only cited from prior work.
Stitching, relative representations, and alignment without paired anchors.
Entire version: no neuron, SAE or circuit comparisons.
No variation of neighbour count or of out-of-distribution inputs; there is a single evaluation set (Objaverse-LVIS).
Plateau with scale is not tested. Shared data is not separated from shared objective.

missing.what: Statement that 3D encoder complexity does not improve alignment (PointNet ≈ PointBERT > SparseConv), contrasted with vision–text results
missing.locator: Sec. 5.2, '3D encoder complexity's low impact on alignment'

missing.what: Zero-shot classification top-1 is below 3% for aligned unimodal 3D encoders, vs above 40% for OpenShape
OpenShape with its own CLIP text encoder reaches 0.94 top-5 retrieval by cosine similarity, with no mapping
missing.locator: Sec. 5.2, 'Multi-modal encoders as an upper bound'

missing.what: Text says PointBERT–RoBERTa CKA is 0.04, but Fig. 2 gives 0.01 (0.04 is PointBert–BERT). This inconsistency needs flagging.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 'supports' label is replaced. Unimodal mappability is weak, and the strong multimodal results come from encoders trained to match CLIP, so they bear on V7 rather than V4. Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 values are legible in the text and should replace 'figure only'. Tranche is set to T3 (new modality) rather than T2. Subspace-method rows are the authors' own method, but they are kept because they measure linear mappability between independent encoders.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size, training scale, or capability; model-complexity comparisons do not test whether alignment rises with scale or performance.
The study compares 3D shapes with text, not paired images and captions or vision and language models.
No comparison of models trained from different initializations or of shared features across seeds.
Tests anchor-based affine and CCA-subspace alignment for 3D-text tasks; does not test stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired anchors.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are compared across models.
Compares CKA and task outcomes, but does not systematically vary similarity-measure settings such as neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Tests 3D-text alignment, including comparisons between explicitly multimodal and unimodal encoders; does not isolate shared data from shared objectives or establish a general cause across modalities.

relationships.condition: Unaligned unimodal 3D encoders vs text encoders, and CLIP-trained multimodal 3D encoders
relationships.reason: Unimodal 3D–text CKA is 0.01–0.12 (R2–R4, R6–R8, R10–R12), well below the cited vision–text range. Alignment is highest where training was shared with CLIP (R1 0.31; R25–R30 matching 61–68%).
relationships.display_finding: Unimodal 3D–text CKA was 0.01–0.12, while shared CLIP training yielded the highest alignment, including CKA 0.31 and matching rates of 61–68%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Unaligned unimodal 3D encoders vs text encoders, and CLIP-trained multimodal 3D encoders
source_check.reason: Unimodal alignment is weak and incomplete; OpenShape–CLIP alignment is higher, which the authors attribute to explicit alignment during training. This supports partial convergence and a training-objective explanation without establishing a causal decomposition.

relationships.condition: Independently trained unimodal 3D encoders mapped to text encoders (CLIP text) with affine, local CKA or CCA-subspace linear maps
relationships.reason: Linear maps raise CKA only to 0.22–0.37 (R14–R24). Matching reaches only 3–18% (R31–R36, R43–R48), or 19–31% with CCA subspaces (R37–R42, R49–R54), far below the multimodal upper bound.
relationships.display_finding: Linear mapping raised CKA to 0.22–0.37, with matching at 3–18% or 19–31% using CCA subspaces, far below the multimodal upper bound.

relationships.condition: Same 3D–text encoder pairs evaluated with global vs subspace-restricted alignment and different methods
relationships.reason: Measured alignment depends on method and subspace: PointBert–CLIP rises from global CKA 0.12 and 15.8% affine matching (R31) to 30.8% with a 50-d CCA subspace (R37). Affine ranks best for matching, local CKA for retrieval (R37–R54). The optimal dimension is encoder-dependent (Fig. 8, text).
relationships.display_finding: PointBert–CLIP had global CKA of 0.12, while affine matching rose from 15.8% to 30.8% using a 50-dimensional CCA subspace; affine alignment ranked best for matching and local CKA for retrieval, with optimal dimension varying by encoder.

reader_labels.reason: Authors describe naive and existing alignment as limited; the reported unimodal results remain below multimodal performance, and alignment requires paired anchors and selected subspaces; see R31-R48.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Unaligned 3D-text encoders and comparison of explicitly multimodal with unimodal encoders
reader_labels.reason: Unaligned unimodal 3D-text CKA is described as weak, while multimodal encoders trained with cross-modal objectives show the strongest alignment and task performance; see R1-R12 and R25-R30.
